judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a checkbox conversion block whose options ('Balance of term insurance — Retain / Cancel', 'Beneficiary on new policy: Same as original policy' vs 'Proceeds payable in accordance with designation of beneficiary (Form 3116) attached') are mutually exclusive alternatives with no marked election on the face of the form, so what was actually requested is genuinely indeterminate. The compressed 'Units / Years' and 'Change to Non-Smoker / Select Non-Smoker' entries sit inside the same block without a governing sentence, leaving their reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Beneficiary-on-new-policy here has to be reconciled with the loan block's 'Beneficiary — Same as original policy / Per Form 3116 attached' (c005) and with paragraph 2)'s rule that there can be no change in plan or benefits without written agreement (c019), and the form nowhere says which controls. That interaction is a plausible but not clearly demonstrated conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure election of premium mode among annual, semi-annual, quarterly, ABC and 'Other', with the requirements expressly cross-referenced to CMAPP Section 03; the only softness is the open-ended 'Other (specify)'. Nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings once a box is checked.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the 'Premium Payment Mode' line in the item 1 conversion block, but the two are alternative paths (conversion vs. change) rather than contradictory commands. No operative provision elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A yes/no question ('Is converted or changed policy to be assigned?') with a conditional instruction to submit new assignment forms; the terms are plain and the consequence of 'yes' is procedural only. It does not say what happens to an existing assignment if the box is left blank, which is a modest gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against the loan block's automatic assignment of 'all right, title and interest' to Ohio National as security (c005) and against the Assignee's Consent line at the foot of the form, which together could make an assignment exist without this box being checked. That is a real but unlitigated tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare heading and checkbox with no operative words at all; its content is supplied entirely by the option table beneath it (Regular Option, Marriage, Birth or Adoption). There is almost nothing here to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the guaranteed purchase option terms of the underlying policy, which are not reproduced in this instrument, but no provision of the form contradicts it. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence 'On full or gross loans, policy loan interest is deducted while loan interest is added to any net loan' turns on the undefined and easily confused trio 'full', 'gross' and 'net' loan, and 'Cash (Amount of Check)' versus 'Gross (Amount of Loan)' invites two readings of how much the owner receives. The interest rate is left to 'the manner set forth in the [policy]', so the operative figure is outside the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic assignment of 'all right, title and Interest on the policy ... to Ohio National as sole security' sits awkwardly with the separate assignment question in c003 and with the Assignee's Consent line, and its closing 'subject to all terms of the policy' subordinates it to a document not before the reader. A conflict is arguable but not squarely established.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Change basic amount from $252000 to $___' states the old face amount but leaves the new one blank, so the very operative number the clause exists to fix is missing — a mechanical defect that changes what the provision means. A dispute over the death benefit would turn directly on this blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also runs into paragraph 2)'s statement that 'there can be no change [in] amount, age at issue, risk, plan or benefits unless I agree to it in writing' (c019) and into the Home Office Endorsement box, since an unfilled amount cannot be the amount agreed in writing. That is a specific, nameable relational problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Change from type ___ to type ___' with both blanks empty and 'type' left undefined; on its face it accomplishes nothing and its scope cannot be determined. But an unchecked, unfilled election is more likely inert than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with items 3 and 6 (change of amount, change to paid-up insurance) and with paragraph 2)'s bar on changes of 'plan or benefits' without written agreement, but no direct contradiction appears. Modest relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement question asks whether insurance is 'intended to serve as a replacement, in whole or in part, of any existing [insurance] or annuities' — 'in part' and 'replacement' are notoriously elastic, but the question is regulatory boilerplate whose answer is factual rather than construed. The follow-on instruction to give company name and policy number is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the form addresses replacement, so there is nothing for it to conflict with. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-line election contrasting the net '{Amount of check}' with 'Gross (Amount of withdrawal including charges)'; the terms are opposed but each is defined in the parenthetical, so the distinction is spelled out rather than left open. The fragment carries no independent operative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the identical cash/gross mechanic in the loan block (c005) and is consistent with it. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A procedural instruction telling the owner which of boxes A and B to check for federal income tax withholding; the operative choice is binary and the boxes are separately spelled out below. Nothing in it bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Box A and Box B elections (c014, c016) and the 20% default for a missing Social Security number (c017), and those are consistent with it rather than contrary. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative sentence — 'Any additional benefit provision attached to this policy shall terminate according to its terms unless otherwise provided' — leaves 'unless otherwise provided' without an identified source, and the paid-up amount is a blank. 'Additional benefit provision' is not defined anywhere on the form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic termination of attached benefit provisions sits directly against item 8's separate mechanism for cancelling Supplementary Agreements (c015) and against paragraph 2)'s bar on changes to 'benefits' without the owner's written agreement (c019). That overlap is a genuine, nameable relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a tax notice: the owner remains liable for federal income tax on 'the taxable portion' of the distribution and may face estimated-tax penalties if withholding is inadequate. 'Taxable portion' is fixed by the Internal Revenue Code, not by this instrument, so there is little for a court to construe in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps textually with c011's paid-up election because the two are interleaved on the page, but as substance the tax notice contradicts nothing else in the form. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Remove or reduce rating' with future monthly insurance costs 'charged based on the reduced or removed rating' is a single, self-consistent rule; 'rating' is a term of art in life underwriting with a settled meaning. The provision does not say when the reduction takes effect, which is a small gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with paragraph 2), which forbids changes in 'risk' classification without written agreement (c019), but the request itself is the owner's written agreement, so they harmonise. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line election — 'I do not want to have Federal income tax withheld from my distribution' — that is as definite as a contract term gets. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by c012's warning of continuing tax liability and by c017's mandatory 20% withholding where no Social Security number is given, which limits but does not contradict it. Some tension with c017 exists but it reads as a stated exception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare instruction to cancel listed Supplementary Agreements with the list left blank; 'Supplementary Agreement' is undefined on the form and the blank means no agreement is actually identified. That combination is a real but small defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the automatic-termination language for 'any additional benefit provision attached to this policy' in c011, and the form never says whether a rider is a Supplementary Agreement, an additional benefit provision, or both. That is a nameable incoherence between two operative items.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line affirmative withholding election; the words are plain and admit of one meaning. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of c014 and consistent with the instructions in c010 and the default rule in c017. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A default rule that a missing owner Social Security number triggers 20% withholding; the trigger and the consequence are both specific and numerical. The only softness is whether it overrides an election, which the sentence does not expressly say.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Box A (c014), which lets the owner elect no withholding at all, this imposes withholding regardless — an arguable direct conflict, though the natural reading is that c017 is a stated exception to c014. Worth noting but not strong.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation that no bankruptcy proceedings, attachment, tax or other lien claim is pending against the owner; the categories are enumerated and closed by a general 'or other lien claim', which is the classic catch-all-against-specifics posture but on a narrow subject. The representation is factual and its consequence is nowhere stated in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands beside paragraphs 2) and 3) as one of the three signature-block undertakings and contradicts none of them; nothing elsewhere on the form addresses liens or creditors except the loan security assignment in c005. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It first deems the owner to ratify any correction made and noted by Ohio National under 'Home Office Endorsement', then flatly bars any change in 'amount, age at issue, risk, plan or benefits unless I agree to it in writing' — the line between a unilateral 'correction' and a prohibited 'change' is exactly the kind of boundary a court would be asked to draw. 'Correction' is undefined and the two halves of the sentence pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the 'FOR HOME OFFICE ENDORSEMENT ONLY — ENDORSE BY ATTACHMENT effective December 1995' box, which lets the insurer alter the request by attachment, and against item 3's change of basic amount (c006), whose new figure is blank; if the endorsement supplied the amount, the writing requirement here is contradicted. That is a specific, nameable conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If any part of the policy is cancelled by a change, Ohio National will be released from any claims or liability under such part' turns on the undefined phrase 'any part of the policy' and on what counts as cancellation 'by a change', and 'premium adjustments will then be made' says nothing about direction, amount or timing. A releasing clause drafted wholly in the insurer's favour on a printed form is also a candidate for construction against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with c011 (attached benefit provisions terminate 'according to its terms unless otherwise provided') and with c019's bar on changes to benefits without written agreement, since this paragraph releases the insurer for cancellations the owner may never have agreed to. That combination is the strongest relational tension on the form.
